edges.effect_quant: Across preschool and mixed-age datasets, fluoride toothpaste consistently lowers caries risk versus placebo or no fluoride. A meta-analysis in preschool children found significant prevention signals in pooled surface-level comparisons, and a three-arm randomized trial showed a concentration-response pattern favoring higher sodium fluoride content for clinical caries reduction.
edges.population: children and adults using fluoride toothpaste for routine home oral hygiene
edges.mechanism: Fluoride toothpaste promotes remineralization of early enamel lesions, reduces demineralization during acid exposure, and can improve the balance between mineral loss and repair during repeated daily brushing.
edges.summary: This is a credible preventive oral-health edge. Fluoride toothpaste has long-standing randomized and synthesized support for lowering caries burden, with stronger protection generally seen at higher fluoride concentrations when adherence is similar.
edges.caveats: Effect sizes vary by age, baseline fluoride exposure, diet, brushing frequency, and concentration used. Much of the hard-outcome literature is older, and benefit at the population level depends on regular use rather than one-off exposure.
